A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dress-ED and Dress-EM. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original VTON/VTOFF experiments in Tables 3–4 and a 221-sample study validating the dataset filtering model in Appendix D.2.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds forward-versus-inverse editing results and a commercial-model comparison in Appendix C, Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: The dataset-generation pipeline, Dress-EM's MLLM–connector–DiT architecture, diffusion objective, and training with both original and edited targets remain unchanged. The new appendix experiments do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Appendix C extends quantitative testing to forward editing with real inputs and synthetic targets, alongside the synthetic-input inverse tests reported in v1. This adds an evaluation scenario within the same Dress-ED dataset, three garment categories, seven edit types, and VTON/VTOFF tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds GPT-Image-1.5 as an evaluated comparator on a 100-sample paired VTON subset in Table 7. The four original comparators remain unchanged. Table 4's FLUX.1 Klein label becomes FLUX.2 Klein, consistent with the existing method description and unchanged scores.

E3.justification: v3 adds a paired forward-versus-inverse evaluation and a commercial comparison on a random 100-sample paired VTON subset, reporting four existing reference metrics. The original 132,201/14,259 training/test split, image resolution, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds a targeted analysis of editing direction to investigate whether performance reflects reversal of synthetic artifacts. The existing per-edit-type analysis and filtering user study are retained; no model-component ablation is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional tables retain point-estimate reporting; the random 100-sample subset does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 6–7 add forward-editing scores and subset-specific commercial comparison results, including SSIM 0.9437 for Dress-EM versus 0.9323 for GPT-Image-1.5. Tables 3–4 and the filtering study are unchanged. Section 3.2 and Table 2 correct 146,640 samples to 146,460, matching the unchanged component counts and splits.

T1.justification: The dataset definitions, generation equations, denoising formulation, and diffusion objective are retained. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first unified instruction-driven VTON/VTOFF dataset, an automated curation pipeline, and a unified diffusion baseline. Replacing approximate 140k references with 146k aligns existing descriptions without changing the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets similar forward/inverse scores as evidence of semantic editing rather than artifact reversal, and attributes resistance to synthetic-distribution collapse to mixed supervision. It also interprets the commercial comparison as supporting domain-specific training. Existing limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link and a direct FASHN parser URL, but removes explicit promises to release code/data, segmentation maps, and template mappings. Implementation settings are retained. The PDFs establish changes to access information, not actual online resource availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, novelty positioning, and set of 72 referenced works remain unchanged. Voost's publication venue and other bibliographic details are updated without introducing or removing cited research.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited terminology and grammar corrections, updates author order, affiliations, and acknowledgments, and inserts an Additional Quantitative Results appendix. Later appendices are relabeled, while the main narrative and existing appendix discussions remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 6–7, adjusts table spacing and Table 2's caption placement, and relocates existing appendix figures through page reflow. Colored cross-references and bibliography backlinks are added. Existing scientific illustrations and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–7 add useful evidence about editing direction and an additional commercial baseline, while corrected dataset counts and labels improve clarity. These are limited gains: the commercial comparison uses only 100 samples, direction similarity does not establish the claimed mechanism, and the new project link accompanies removal of more explicit release commitments.
